key_concept: A carbocation's empty $p$ orbital is stabilized only by donation of electron density from adjacent filled orbitals: filled $\pi$ orbitals (resonance) and filled $\sigma_{C-H}$ orbitals (hyperconjugation).
steps: Identify the species: $C_6H_5-\overset{+}{C}H-CH_3$ is a secondary benzylic carbocation. Its cationic carbon is $sp^2$ hybridised and carries a vacant $2p$ orbital.

An empty orbital is stabilized only when a neighbouring orbital donates electron density into it. Interaction with another empty orbital ($\sigma^*$ or $\pi^*$) transfers no electrons, so it gives no stabilization.

Resonance: the vacant $p$ orbital overlaps with the filled $\pi$ orbitals of the benzene ring. This delocalises the positive charge onto the ortho and para positions. This is a filled $\pi \rightarrow$ empty $p$ interaction.

Hyperconjugation: the $CH_3$ group has three $\alpha$-$C-H$ bonds. Their filled $\sigma_{C-H}$ orbitals overlap with the empty $p$ orbital, giving 3 hyperconjugative structures. This is a filled $\sigma \rightarrow$ empty $p$ interaction.
So the carbocation is stabilized by filled $\sigma$ and filled $\pi$ orbitals, which is option (1).
why_not_others: Options (2), (3) and (4) all include an empty orbital ($\sigma$, $\sigma^*$ or $\pi^*$). An empty orbital has no electrons to donate to the vacant $p$ orbital, so it cannot stabilize the cation. Option (3) is also wrong because it pairs empty $\sigma^*$ with filled $\pi$; the $\sigma^*$ interaction applies to carbanions or negative hyperconjugation, not to carbocations.
common_trap: Students recall '$\sigma \rightarrow \sigma^*$' or '$\pi^*$' from hyperconjugation and back-bonding discussions and wrongly pick an option containing antibonding orbitals, forgetting that a cation needs an electron donor.
time_saving_tip: Empty orbital needs electrons, so the stabilizing orbitals must be filled. Only option (1) contains filled orbitals alone, so you can mark it immediately.
